changes.before: Step 0 of the tool determines the review track from two facts the policy names: how long the effects last, and the highest approval level the action needs. Lasting effect plus supervisor-or-above approval means a formal equity analysis is required and must accompany the action when it goes for approval. An equity scan is appropriate only when the action already went through a formal analysis and those results were integrated. A short timeline is never, by itself, a reason to scan. When in doubt, ask the ADSA Equity Director; the policy gives that role the authority to advise and to provide an approved analysis for the administration.
changes.after: Step 0 identifies the policy criterion from the expected duration of the effects and the approval level. An action with prolonged or long-term impact scheduled for approval at supervisor level or above requires formal equity analysis. The policy allows a DHS Equity Analysis, an Equity Scan, or a customized tool developed in consultation with the equity director to accompany the action. Use the official Toolkit User Guide and consult the responsible equity office to determine the appropriate approach. A short timeline or a prior analysis alone does not settle that choice. The tool does not approve the review or replace these responsibilities.

changes.before: Decision-maker and decision date are named, and the review track was determined from impact and approval level.
changes.after: Decision-maker and decision date are named, and review questions are answered. Confirm the appropriate review with the official User Guide and responsible equity office.

changes.before: Step 0 asks what you are analyzing, what kind of action it is, who is responsible, who will decide, and when. Then three questions determine the review track: how long the effects last, the highest approval level, and whether a formal analysis was already done. As soon as all three are answered, a box appears stating the track: a formal equity analysis required, or an equity scan likely sufficient. The same track appears in the left column so it stays visible on every step. Changing any of the three answers updates it at once.
changes.after: Step 0 records the action, responsible people, decision date, expected duration and approval level, together with any earlier review. Once the action type, duration and approval level are entered, the tool identifies whether the policy criterion for a prolonged or long-term action scheduled for leadership approval is met. Otherwise it prompts you to confirm review requirements. It does not decide that an equity scan is sufficient. Use the official Toolkit User Guide and responsible equity office to confirm the appropriate approach. The review message stays visible in the left column and updates when the action type, duration or approval level changes.
